ordered_diagnoses: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with cerebrovascular and cognitive manifestations
salient_findings: Brisk bilateral tendon reflexes and bilateral Babinski sign
Lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI
Multiple cerebral microbleeds with lobe-dominant distribution on susceptibility-weighted imaging
key_facts: 2-year history of headache, dizziness, and imbalance
History of hypertension
History of cervical disc herniation
Underwent transcatheter closure for patent foramen ovale one year ago
Family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance
Father died of cerebral hemorrhage at age 65
Neurological examination revealed brisk bilateral tendon reflexes and bilateral Babinski sign
MRI showed lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities
Susceptibility-weighted imaging showed multiple cerebral microbleeds
Heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene

shortlist.label: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of progressive cognitive decline and imbalance, and presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI

shortlist.label: HTRA1-related hereditary vascular amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Heterozygous mutation (c.754G>A, p.A252T) in the HTRA1 gene, and presence of cerebral microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging

shortlist.label: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of cerebral microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging, and family history of cerebral hemorrhage

shortlist.label: CARASIL syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation to CADASIL, with presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI

shortlist.label: Col4A1-related cerebral small vessel disease
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities on MRI, and potential for familial inheritance

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous mutation in the HTRA1 gene, along with the patient's symptoms of headache, dizziness, and imbalance, and the imaging findings of lacunar infarctions and periventricular white matter hyperintensities, are consistent with CARASIL syndrome, which is caused by mutations in the HTRA1 gene and typically presents with these features.

rejected.label: Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy (CADASIL)
rejected.why: CADASIL is typically associated with NOTCH3 gene mutations, not HTRA1 gene mutations.

rejected.label: HTRA1-related hereditary vascular amyloidosis
rejected.why: While the HTRA1 gene mutation is present, the clinical and imaging features are more consistent with CARASIL syndrome than with HTRA1-related hereditary vascular amyloidosis.

rejected.label: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy
rejected.why: Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy is typically associated with amyloid beta deposition, which is not mentioned in the case, and the imaging findings are not typical for this condition.

rejected.label: Col4A1-related cerebral small vessel disease
rejected.why: There is no mention of a COL4A1 gene mutation, and the clinical and imaging features are more consistent with CARASIL syndrome.
